rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with the reported 4BA and identifies a hatching/expanded blastocyst with looser ICM and stronger TE, but the image is low-contrast and some specifics (e.g., protruding tissue, continuous epithelial rim, zona comments) are somewhat overcalled from what is clearly visible.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometrial thickness, BMI, first-cycle status, and male-factor semen parameters with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is mostly logical and structured, but there is an internal inconsistency: it first gives live birth around 35–50% per transfer, then states 'mid-to-high teens percent,' which conflicts with the earlier estimate.

Largely aligned with standard IVF practice: accepts 4BA as a good transfer embryo, avoids unsupported add-ons, and appropriately notes PGT-A is not mandatory at age 31. Minor overemphasis on sperm DNA concerns without stronger case-specific evidence.

Provides practical recommendations for proceeding with transfer, luteal support review, lifestyle optimization, and future male-factor/workup considerations, though some advice remains somewhat general rather than protocol-specific.
